items.stem: Why is loading large classical datasets into a quantum computer a central challenge for quantum machine learning?

options.text: Encoding many data points into quantum states can cost as much as the computation you hoped to speed up
options.rationale: Correct: the data-loading/input bottleneck can erase any theoretical speedup for data-heavy tasks.

options.text: Quantum computers cannot represent numbers at all
options.rationale: They can represent amplitudes; the issue is the cost of loading, not representation.

options.text: Classical data must first be deleted to free qubits
options.rationale: This is not how encoding works; data is mapped into states, not deleted.

options.text: Loading data is instantaneous so it is never a concern
options.rationale: Loading is often the dominant cost, not instantaneous.

items.explanation: Correct: the data-loading/input bottleneck can erase any theoretical speedup for data-heavy tasks.

items.stem: Which TWO are genuine near-term limitations of variational quantum machine learning? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Barren plateaus can make gradients vanish and training stall
options.rationale: Correct: barren plateaus are a well-documented trainability problem.

options.text: Noise on NISQ hardware degrades the quality of the learned model
options.rationale: Correct: device noise is a major constraint on today's variational models.

options.text: Variational circuits are proven to beat all classical models
options.rationale: No such general proof exists; advantage is problem-specific and unproven in general.

options.text: They require no classical computation at all
options.rationale: They are hybrid: a classical optimiser updates the circuit parameters.

items.explanation: Correct: barren plateaus are a well-documented trainability problem.

items.stem: A pilot reports a quantum classifier reached 82% accuracy. What is the most important follow-up before claiming success?

options.text: Compare it against a strong classical baseline on the same data and splits
options.rationale: Correct: without a classical baseline the number says nothing about quantum advantage.

options.text: Add more qubits because accuracy always rises with qubit count
options.rationale: Accuracy does not reliably rise with qubit count; baselines matter more.

options.text: Publish immediately since 82% is above random
options.rationale: Being above random is not evidence of advantage over classical methods.

options.text: Remove the classical optimiser to make it 'fully quantum'
options.rationale: Variational QML needs the classical optimiser; removing it is not a validity check.

items.explanation: Correct: without a classical baseline the number says nothing about quantum advantage.
